claims.claim_text: CircuitPython is a fork of MicroPython created by Adafruit; the fork was motivated by the absence of a consistent hardware API across the boards MicroPython supported.
claims.quote_verbatim: it wasn't clear to me that there was a consistent story across all of the boards that they supported
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: The fork's stated goal was a uniform hardware foundation across every target platform.
claims.quote_verbatim: we wanted to ensure that we had a foundation that was uniform across all of the places we could bring circuit Python
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: MicroPython is a Python implementation for microcontrollers; Adafruit compiled it for the Atmel SAMD family and renamed the result, with a more hardware-specific focus.
claims.quote_verbatim: Adafruit took that and then specifically for the, the Atmel, SamD family started compiling it for that
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: CircuitPython compiles source to bytecode once, up front, rather than reinterpreting source at runtime.
claims.quote_verbatim: CircuitPython will translate your source code to byte code up front
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: The binary flashed to a board is machine code containing the virtual machine plus the board's pin data structures; per-board builds are published as GitHub releases.
claims.quote_verbatim: that will be the machine code that has all of the VM and, and all of the data structures to tell you what pin is what
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: A CircuitPython board enumerates as a USB mass-storage device carrying editable example code; editing and saving the file runs it, with no separate flashing step.
claims.quote_verbatim: it will show up as a USB drive and it will have example code on it in a file called code.py
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: The edit-save-run loop replaces the compile-and-upload cycle, with the board soft-rebooting on save.
claims.quote_verbatim: I open up the main.py. I, I edit it. I hit save. It's soft reboots
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Because code is interpreted on the device, iteration does not require erasing and reprogramming the chip.
claims.quote_verbatim: now you're not erasing the entire chip compiling and then uploading it all back
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: The entry file is named code.py, and code.txt is also accepted, on the assumption that target users may not know what Python or a main function is.
claims.quote_verbatim: we call it code.py and we actually support calling the file code.text as well
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: CircuitPython deliberately accepts lower execution performance than MicroPython in exchange for closer CPython compatibility, so that existing Python documentation and idioms transfer.
claims.quote_verbatim: we've, we've explicitly chosen to be less performant than MicroPython in order to be more similar to Python
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: The design optimises iteration time rather than execution speed, on the argument that short iteration is what beginners need.
claims.quote_verbatim: it may not be the fastest to execute, but it's really fast to iterate
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: Code-generation wizards of the Atmel Start or STM32Cube type are unsuited to CircuitPython, because the runtime is dynamic and neither user code nor pin assignment is known at build time.
claims.quote_verbatim: we don't know the code that the user is going to write and we don't know what pin they're going to want to use for something
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: Hardware support began with the Atmel SAMD21 and SAMD51 and extended to Nordic nRF51 and nRF52 parts.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's the Adafruit version of MicroPython specific to the, to the SAMD 2151 chipsets and now NRF 51, 52
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: CircuitPython libraries can run unmodified on a desktop host and then be redeployed to a Raspberry Pi or a CircuitPython board.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can use those same Python libraries without any modifications from your, you know, your desktop, your windows, your Mac, your, your Linux PC
claims.speaker: Jonathan Georgino

claims.claim_text: From 2018 the project was defined to include its guides, API reference documentation, driver support, Discord community and code of conduct, not only the installed runtime.
claims.quote_verbatim: It includes the guides, it includes the API reference docs, it includes the driver support
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: Removing the IDE and driver installation eliminates the most common category of beginner support request, since installation and COM-port problems dominate vendor support email.
claims.quote_verbatim: software questions like instillation and comports are like number one questions you get
claims.speaker: Ken Burns

claims.claim_text: The project targets people who have never programmed, and decisions are not optimised for users arriving from Arduino, MicroPython or C.
claims.quote_verbatim: our goal is to be an excellent experience for people who have never programmed in their life
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: Assumed before the interview that the fork was motivated by hardware focus rather than by audience mission.
claims.quote_verbatim: I thought it was because of the hardware focus of it all. But I actually like this mission based
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Dismissed CircuitPython on first mention as one more entrant in a crowded field of development platforms.
claims.quote_verbatim: This is just like the 50th. 50th different. Development platform. To come along in the last five years.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Declined to learn CircuitPython on the grounds that learning it would dissipate the enthusiasm that starts a project.
claims.quote_verbatim: I just want to do something while I'm excited. And that does not include learning circuit Python
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Recommended CircuitPython while acknowledging it contradicted his own prior position against interpreted languages on hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: Contradicts my whole thing about JavaScript on hardware
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: By 2018 expressed confidence in CircuitPython and MicroPython for real work, a reversal from a year earlier.
claims.quote_verbatim: I am feeling relatively confident about circuit Python these days
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Revised a long-held dismissal of simplified programming interfaces, on the grounds that each new platform imposes a fresh learning cost.
claims.quote_verbatim: every time there's a new platform, you got to learn the new thing
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Supports CircuitPython as a market observation about non-engineer users rather than a personal preference, describing himself as an embedded developer who would choose C.
claims.quote_verbatim: again, the embedded guy
claims.speaker: Ken Burns

claims.claim_text: Characterised Adafruit's leadership as having committed to MicroPython and CircuitPython as the company's future platform.
claims.quote_verbatim: Lamore and Phil have really bet on MicroPython and, and CircuitPython as a platform for the future
claims.speaker: Scott Shawcroft

claims.claim_text: Storing source on the device itself removes the loss mode in which an undo-less editing session leaves a previously working project unrecoverable.
claims.quote_verbatim: the thing that was working the first 30 times and on the 31st time I changed something that I don't remember
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The similarity between the MicroPython and CircuitPython names is a schedule risk in itself; confusing them cost a deadline on an RP2040 project.
claims.quote_verbatim: I didn't know circuit Python and micro Python were different. So I just blew my deadline
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Reality Instruments' commercial boards were built on CircuitPython specifically so that end users would find them easy to program.
claims.quote_verbatim: I wanted to have circuit Python available for, for people. So it's just as easy for people using it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: By 2022 CircuitPython ran on Espressif's ESP32-S2 breakout boards, which also removed the need for an external USB-to-UART converter.
claims.quote_verbatim: It actually runs CircuitPython as well
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: By 2021 CircuitPython was in use in US middle-school technology teaching.
claims.quote_verbatim: he's using circuit Python, which is the Adafruit one, not micro Python
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The Adafruit Trinket M0 ships with CircuitPython preinstalled and was the board that prompted the hosts' first sustained use.
claims.quote_verbatim: So I do recommend trying it out at least
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
